name: Smear
description: Smear (also spelled 'Schmier' or 'Schmear') is a card game played in the northern Midwest of the USA (Minnesota, Wisconsin), closely related to Pitch and High-Low-Jack. It is a trick-taking game typically played with 4 players in partnerships. The objective is to score points for High, Low, Jack, and Game (the 'Smear'), with bids usually starting at 2 or 3. The term 'Smear' also refers to the act of playing a high-point card (like a 10 or Ace) on a partner's winning trick.

content.text: Smear (also spelled 'Schmier' or 'Schmear') is a card game played in the northern Midwest of the USA (Minnesota, Wisconsin), closely related to Pitch and High-Low-Jack. It is a trick-taking game typically played with 4 players in partnerships. The objective is to score points for High, Low, Jack, and Game (the 'Smear'), with bids usually starting at 2 or 3. The term 'Smear' also refers to the act of playing a high-point card (like a 10 or Ace) on a partner's winning trick.
Derived from All Fours and Pitch, with a focus on team play and aggressive point-dumping (smearing). The name comes from the German word 'schmieren' (to grease or bribe).
Four players in fixed partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other. Some variants use six players in two teams of three or three players without partners.

Standard 52-card pack; cards in each suit rank A, K, Q, J, 10 down to 2. Some variants use a 54-card pack with one or two jokers as extra trumps, or a stripped 32-card deck (A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7 per suit).

items.text: Ten Point Smear: 10 points per hand with Jick (left bower) and two jokers; bids 4 to 10; played to 52. Four, five, or six players.
Wisconsin Six Point: 32-card deck (A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7) plus two jokers; 6 points; low to holder of lowest trump other than joker; target usually 21.
